usageNotes: Use this to remove a specific IP address, network CIDR, or alias from a named IPSet on a VM's firewall. The operation returns null synchronously — no UPID is issued — so changes take effect immediately without polling. The caller must hold the VM.Config.Network privilege on /vms/{vmid}, and the target IPSet must already exist; deleting the last entry from an IPSet does not auto-delete the IPSet itself.

examples.summary: Remove 10.10.20.0/24 from the 'trusted-mgmt' IPSet on VM 105

destructiveReason: Permanently removes the specified IP/CIDR entry from the IPSet; any firewall rules that relied on this entry to permit or deny traffic will immediately stop matching it, potentially exposing or blocking access without further warning.
tips: Pass the 'digest' query parameter (obtained from the IPSet GET response) to guard against concurrent edits overwriting each other.
If you need to remove all entries from an IPSet before deleting the set itself, enumerate entries first via the corresponding GET endpoint and delete them one by one.
The 'cidr' path segment must exactly match the stored value (e.g., '10.0.0.1' and '10.0.0.1/32' are treated as distinct entries).
Aliases (e.g., '+datacenter') are valid 'cidr' values when the IPorCIDRorAlias format is used — match the alias name exactly as stored.
